review.summary: Phase 28 readiness is genuinely built, not renamed: phase-28 commands = full phase-27 set plus two `--require-directional` clean-package qualifications and `check-access-release --phase 28 --version 0.2.4`, all 105 commands executed at exit 0 in one continuous run bound to source 5156a408, with `--resume` barred for phase 28. `--require-directional` is a real constraint with negative coverage; the delivery branch (registry/tag/49 CI contexts) exists and fails closed; a readiness review cannot advance. Dependency audit is fresh and clean; live acceptance is honestly bounded. Blocking the 46/50 bar: the packaged README still names 0.1.1 as the published release and tells consumers to install 0.2.0 while 0.2.3 is published, and that README is bound by `readmeSha256` in the readiness receipt. Four supportability/doc lows remain unaddressed from the chunk review.

findings.description: README misstates the current published release inside a packaged archive member. Line 29 says "The published maintenance release is [0.1.1]", line 35 says "Install the vendor update as scm-sdk 0.2.0", and lines 51-52 tell consumers to "retain your existing released pin" without naming it. docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.3.json (version 0.2.3, yanked false, publishedAt 2026-10-20) and docs/phase-status.json:6689-6693 (status published_and_verified) show 0.2.3 is the published release, and docs/STABILITY.md:31 says so. Cargo.toml include ships README.md, and docs/checks/phase-28-release-readiness.json:23-26,703 binds its bytes, so publishing 0.2.4 would ship install guidance pointing at 0.2.0. The automated guard cannot catch this: tools/test_ci.py:346-348 returns early because workspace version 0.2.4 != publication version 0.2.3.
findings.required_fix: Name 0.2.3 as the current verified published release in README.md and cite docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.3.json (matching docs/STABILITY.md:31), replace the 0.2.0 install line, then re-run scripts/check-management-package.py --require-directional for both toolchains and scripts/check-access-release.py --phase 28 --version 0.2.4 so the readiness receipt rebinds the corrected readmeSha256 and archives.

findings.description: The maintenance section gives explicit acceptance paragraphs for phase 26 (278-281) and phase 27 (283-289) but none for phase 28; it only states that phase 28 "gates its release and delivery" and that package consumers are deferred to it. AGENTS.md:3 makes PHASES.md the document to read before implementation or review, yet phase 28's actual requirements (both-compiler directional consumers, version-specific 0.2.4 readiness guard, registry/tag/49 CI contexts, readiness cannot complete the phase) appear only in docs/RELEASE.md:188-203, docs/CI.md:339-346 and the plan.
findings.required_fix: Add a phase-28 acceptance paragraph to docs/PHASES.md mirroring the 26/27 entries: both named chunks, the version-specific 0.2.4 guards, and the exact delivery evidence required.

findings.description: The "TypeScript 0.35.0 patch release (phase 28)" section documents only check_phase.py and check-prepublication.py. Unlike the 0.2.3 procedure (lines 53-61, 49-50) it omits the 0.2.4 forms of scripts/verify-publication.py with docs/checks/phase-28-release-package-1.99.0.json / -1.89.0.json, scripts/observe-release.py --version 0.2.4, and tools/release_delivery.py --phase 28 --version 0.2.4. It also never states that publication must be performed with the 1.99.0 toolchain, even though scripts/verify-publication.py:106-110 requires the registry checksum to equal the 1.99.0 proof's archive_sha256 and docs/checks/phase-28-release-readiness.json:704 binds 447ca402 (the 1.99.0 archive, distinct from the 1.89.0 archive 14f0292f).
findings.required_fix: Extend docs/RELEASE.md:188-203 with the exact 0.2.4 verify-publication, observe-release and release_delivery invocations and state that the registry archive must be produced by the 1.99.0 toolchain bound in the readiness receipt.

findings.description: The interrupted-qualification section documents --resume for "active phases 23–25" only, while tools/check_phase.py:893,895 permit 23, 24, 25 and 27. The deliberate exclusion of phase 28 (so release readiness cannot be assembled from a checkpointed prefix, and there is no docs/checks/phase-28-partial.json) is a meaningful property that is not documented anywhere.
findings.required_fix: Update docs/CI.md:327-337 to state the actual permitted set (23–25 and 27) and record that phase 28 requires a single complete run with no checkpoint reuse.

findings.description: A conditional expression is used as a bare statement at the directional enforcement point: `wrapper.verify_receipt(root, path, compiler, require_directional=True) if phase == 28 else wrapper.verify_receipt(root, path, compiler)`. Both branches are side-effecting calls whose return value is discarded, which obscures that this single line is what makes the phase-28 readiness guard directional and invites an edit that silently drops the flag.
findings.required_fix: Replace with one call: `wrapper.verify_receipt(root, path, compiler, require_directional=phase == 28)`.

findings.description: CONTRACT_CI_PHASES was extended with 28 (line 136) but the --contracts-only diagnostic still reads "requires --phase 12 --verification-only (or another supported phase: 17, 20, 21–25)", omitting 28. The CI workflow (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:73) runs exactly `--phase 28 --verification-only --contracts-only`, so the error text now misdescribes the supported set a maintainer would consult after a typo.
findings.required_fix: Update the parser.error message at tools/check_phase.py:898 to list the actual CONTRACT_CI_PHASES set including 28, ideally derived from the constant.

findings.description: The advisory gate audits only the root lockfile (`lock_path = ROOT/'Cargo.lock'`, used at line 196 for cargo-audit and lines 208-209 for cargo-deny). contracts/native-probes/Cargo.lock was updated in this phase to the same patched TLS versions (rustls-webpki 0.103.16 at :1123, webpki-root-certs 1.0.10 at :1772) but is never independently audited, so a future advisory affecting only the probe lockfile would not fail the phase-28 dependency check even though that lockfile is consumed by the external package consumers and the native-probes CI feature set.
findings.required_fix: Audit contracts/native-probes/Cargo.lock as a second lockfile input in scripts/check-dependencies.py and record its digest in the receipt, or document in docs/CI.md and docs/DEPENDENCIES.md why the probe lockfile is excluded from the advisory gate.

evidence: Check evidence is real and complete, not a subset: docs/reviews/phase-28-attempt-01.checks.json:1-6 binds phase 28 to source_sha256 5156a408... with passed true and source_unchanged true; 105 recorded commands, every one "exit_code": 0, zero matches for "timeout": true or "source_unchanged": false. tools/review_phase.py:222-228 requires [item['command'] for item in checks] == commands_for(28) with every exit_code == 0, and :232-233 additionally re-verifies checkpoint_bindings for phase 28 on current source.

Phase-28 command set is phase 27 plus exactly three new guards: tools/check_phase.py:318-328 renames phase-27 receipt paths to phase-28 and appends check-management-package.py --require-directional for 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 plus check-access-release.py --phase 28 --version 0.2.4. Those three appear in the executed evidence at checks.json:2862-2891, 2893-2923 and 2924-2955, with checkpoint_bindings to their receipts and to the retained .crate files under .local/package-worktrees/4c85f31e.../.

Execution was a single continuous run, not a checkpoint assembly: first check executed_at 2026-10-22T11:34:18, last 12:53:52; the two package qualifications took 391s and 373s. tools/check_phase.py:892-896 rejects --resume for any phase outside (23,24,25,27), and no docs/checks/phase-28-partial.json exists.

--require-directional is a substantive additional constraint: scripts/check-management-package.py:114 requires exactly 5 external consumer indices (4 without the flag); :152-164 requires examples/directional_profiles.rs in the archive, a digest equal to both the archive member and the working-tree file, selectedFeatures == [], a unique in-range checkIndex executed in the external consumer root, and a separate `run --example directional_profiles --all-features --locked --offline` inside the extracted archive. scripts/check-package.py:175-176,218-223 are the matching producers.

Negative coverage exists for the new guard: tools/test_release_024.py:204-232 verifies the receipt then rejects a wrong sha256, a checkIndex colliding with frozenProbeCheckIndex, selectedFeatures == ['red-team'], and omission of the directional entry. :63-71 pins the exact command set, :103-116 pins archives to the qualified commit worktree, :118-128 pins require_directional through both compiler proofs.

The 0.2.4 readiness receipt is source-bound, not a 0.2.3 copy: scripts/check-access-release.py:30 registers (28,'0.2.4') and rejects (24,'0.2.4') (asserted in tools/test_release_022.py:31-32 and test_release_024.py:28-30); :62 reads phase-28-release-package-{compiler}.json; :67 requires schema 3; :69-71 requires commit_fingerprint(releaseCommit) == fingerprint(root) plus ancestry to HEAD; :82-106 re-derives the archive with the scm-sdk-0.2.4/ prefix and compares every packaged src/examples/README/LICENSE/NOTICE/Cargo.toml.orig byte against both the working tree and `git show releaseCommit:...`; :119-120 requires both compiler proofs to qualify identical files/vcs. Output docs/checks/phase-28-release-readiness.json:4-5,704-708 records 0.2.4, releaseCommit 4c85f31e..., archiveSha256 447ca402..., toolchains [1.89.0, 1.99.0].

The plan-required phase-28 delivery branch exists and fails closed: tools/review_phase.py:483-489 calls release_delivery.verify(..., phase=28, version='0.2.4'); tools/release_delivery.py:22,190 register and enforce the (28,'0.2.4') pair; :203-204 requires docs/checks/phase-28-remote-ci-run-N.json; :226-230 forwards require_directional=True; :104-115 requires CI job contexts to equal the configured matrix exactly with no duplicate target_urls; :142-155 requires the registry receipt to reference an accepted phase-28 readiness review with matching source and review digests.

A readiness review cannot complete the phase: tools/review_phase.py:459-460 forbids --release-readiness with --advance, :478-479 rejects advancement when review_scope != 'phase', and :304 restricts the allowed scopes. tools/test_release_024.py:73-101 exercises both paths and asserts docs/phase-status.json is left unmodified.

CI is wired to this phase with a derived, asserted context set: .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:73 runs `check_phase.py --phase 28 --verification-only --contracts-only`; ci.yml:90-91 declares 2 toolchains x 24 feature sets; tools/release_delivery.py:56-69 derives 48 rust contexts plus contracts-and-package = 49; tools/check_phase.py:136 adds 28 to CONTRACT_CI_PHASES and :813-825 strips every native/package/access-release command from the CI subset (asserted in tools/test_release_024.py:70).

Dependency security is current rather than inherited: docs/checks/phase-28-dependencies.json:3-13,47-52 shows the audit ran at 11:36:58 within this phase run against advisory-db revision 640bf5a9 with freshHead true, 0 vulnerabilities and no warnings; Cargo.lock:1122-1125,1772-1775 and contracts/native-probes/Cargo.lock:1122-1125,1771-1774 both carry rustls-webpki 0.103.16 and webpki-root-certs 1.0.10, matching CHANGELOG.md:37-40. tools/check_phase.py:361-365 moves the audit ahead of the Rust matrix.

Release and live claims are accurate and bounded: CHANGELOG.md:5-6,43-44 state release candidate and that the entry establishes no publication or remote delivery; docs/STABILITY.md:3-5,34; docs/RELEASE.md:3-8,199-202. docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:15-23 records 1 verified method (OAuth), four HTTP 403 permission prerequisites, no mutations, cleanupState not_needed, and "Directional profile create/update remain live-unverified"; contracts/live-evidence.json:4-5 binds docs/checks/phase-28-live-attempt-01.json by digest.

Packaged privacy and compiler evidence were executed on this source: docs/checks/phase-28-private-material.json:3-12 records sourceSha256 5156a408, headCommit 4c85f31e, 2376 git-visible files, 135 packaged src/example candidates, 0 credential and 0 registration value matches; docs/checks/phase-28-rust-1.89.0-management.json:3-15 shows a native musl run on rustc 1.89.0 with the phase lockfile digest e76abae3 matching the dependency receipt.

The delivered consumer is substantive, not a stub: crates/scm-sdk/examples/directional_profiles.rs:13-57 builds the new ContentTypeConfiguration/ContentTypeConfigurations types, round-trips the request through `typescript:0.35.0:CreateSecurityProfileRequestSchema`, and then asserts lossless preservation of a wrong-typed/null response document in both Mode::Response and Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults. contracts/native-probes/Cargo.toml:11 supplies the `management` feature to the external consumer, so the selectedFeatures == [] binding is meaningful.

Chunk disposition: docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-release-readiness-attempt-01.json accepted the release-readiness chunk at 44/50 on this identical source 5156a408 with one medium (README) and four low findings. The source fingerprint has not changed, so none of those findings is yet addressed; I independently confirmed all five and add two more (tools/check_phase.py:898, docs/RELEASE.md:188).
limitations: Read-only review: I executed no commands and re-ran no checks. All pass/fail conclusions rest on reading docs/reviews/phase-28-attempt-01.checks.json and docs/checks/phase-28-*.json and tracing the registered command set in tools/check_phase.py:318-328 against the gate in tools/review_phase.py:201-234. I did not recompute the source fingerprint, any receipt SHA-256, or the retained .crate digests.

I did not open the retained archives under .local/package-worktrees/4c85f31e.../.local/artifacts/ or the extracted consumer roots; directional consumer execution is established by the recorded receipts plus the verification logic in scripts/check-management-package.py:152-164, not by inspecting build output.

Remote delivery is the other phase-28 chunk and is unverified here: no docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.4.json, release-tag-v0.2.4.json or phase-28-remote-ci-run-N.json exists; docs/phase-status.json:8150-8160 milestones are all pending and no registry_publication block exists for phase 28; the 49 CI contexts have not been observed on the released source. Actual registry publication, the remote annotated tag and terminal CI remain pending delivery obligations, not completed outcomes.

Generated model correctness, the additive overlay, the oracle corpus and the schema-graph roots are phase-27 deliverables accepted at 46/50; I relied on this phase's recorded Rust/management receipts and the declaration-level evidence rather than re-auditing crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs or validation/schema_graph.json.

Per instruction I read no credential or tenant-registration material, nothing outside this repository, and no optional .local/typescript checkout; the `verify-contracts.py --baseline .local/typescript` result (extractedBaselineVerified true) is taken from the recorded run.

Phase 24/25 acceptance, the 0.2.3 delivery gate and pre-phase-26 release infrastructure were out of scope beyond the pinned 0.2.3 receipt identity that tools/review_phase.py:409 depends on and the published-0.2.3 facts relevant to the README finding.
This record is the prepublication readiness assessment and cannot advance the phase; a fresh complete-phase review after delivery and both accepted chunks is required.
